verdict: OK to lend in Pune engineering & capital goods — pursue export-linked component makers and asset-light subcontractors with order visibility; avoid leveraged greenfield casters and EPC bidders living on bank guarantees.
title: Pune Engineering & Capital Goods: a note to the credit manager
narrative:
## What this business physically is
**Pune engineering is a conversion business: steel, castings and forgings go in, machined components and sub-assemblies come out, and cash comes back only after the OEM or export buyer accepts the part.** The city's cluster sits around Pimpri-Chinchwad, where the auto cluster exhibition halls host both Subcontract India 2026 (17–19 December, EEPC India, ~5,000 business visitors and 100 overseas buyers advertised) [1] and MOTOTECH 2026, whose opening focused on EV readiness and MSME use of cluster prototyping facilities [3]. Those are organiser-advertised figures, not confirmed attendance [1].

## Where value and cash sit
**Value sits in the machining tolerance and the approved-vendor status, not in the metal; cash sits in receivables and in the bank guarantee.** Peer results show the split: DEE Development Engineers grew revenue 77% YoY to ₹286.7 crore in Q3FY26 with operating profit up more than sevenfold to ₹47.6 crore, largely oil-and-gas piping [5]; Skipper posted its highest-ever Q2 revenue with PAT up 56% [6]; Suzlon grew revenue 26% to ₹4,869 crore but EBITDA stayed near ₹720 crore and margin fell to 14.8% from 18.6% [7]. **Volume growth without margin is the pattern to underwrite against.** Rating commentary flags that EPC cash conversion cycles run longer than OEMs, and that bank guarantees are required for bidding [9][11]. So when a proposal lands, check the receivable days and the non-fund-based limit separately; if the BG line is larger than the term loan, ask what happens to liquidity if one tender is lost.

## What has changed now
**The demand signal is real and national; the Pune-specific read is thin.** India IIP for NIC 28 is +10.3% YoY and +10.4% Apr-to-date, and exports are +19.8% Apr-to-date in USD [D]. Maharashtra GST collections are +8.6% Apr-to-date against India's +6.1% [D]. Local sources are event notices, not order data [1][3] — **treat Pune as first principles plus peers.** Pitti Engineering is commissioning a Hyderabad casting and machining plant in phases through FY2030 on data-centre, mining and railway order visibility [4]; that is where capex risk is building.

## Who to pursue, and how to grow safely
**Pursue tier-2 machining and sub-assembly suppliers with a named OEM or export buyer, and asset-light subcontractors feeding the December Subcontract India buyer meets [1].** Avoid greenfield casting capex and EPC bidders whose order book is unexecuted [4][9]. Structure as a cash-flow loan against assigned receivables, keep BG and LC limits ring-fenced, and covenant a minimum EBITDA margin and receivable days. Take monthly stock-and-receivable statements, quarterly GST returns, and the order-book position every month.

## Early-warning signs
**Watch receivable days stretching past the peer norm, margin slipping while revenue rises (the Suzlon pattern [7]), and BG utilisation climbing without fresh orders.** If a borrower's top buyer share crosses half of revenue, ask for the buyer's payment history before renewal.
watch: Receivable days rise two months running -> cut limit and ask for buyer-wise ageing
GST turnover falls below bank statement credits -> reprice or exit at renewal
Order book falls while BG outstanding rises -> freeze new non-fund limits
Margin falls while revenue grows -> shift to receivable-backed structure
Rating downgrade or outlook change -> reassess collateral cover
watch_note: Trigger levels are policy suggestions (analytical framing), not data.
news_why: National IIP and export data strong; Pune sources are event notices, not order data.
